articles.title: 5 unusual buildings in Barcelona
articles.lead: Barcelona is famous for its architecture, but it also hides lesser-known gems that are just as captivating.
articles.excerpt: From Gothic masterpieces to futuristic landmarks — five unusual Barcelona buildings that surprise even seasoned travellers.
articles.imagePrompt: A twilight panorama of Barcelona’s skyline featuring the soaring Sagrada Família, the undulating curves of Casa Milà, the vibrant mosaics of Park Güell, and the glowing glass façade of Torre Agbar, all bathed in warm sunset light.

sections.title: Sagrada Família: a temple that keeps changing
Park Güell: a fairytale park of mosaics and sculptures
Casa Milà and Bunker Park: from a wave-like house to a hidden underground zone
Torre Agbar: a modern skyscraper that changes colour

body.text: Barcelona is famous for its architecture, but it also hides lesser-known gems that are just as captivating.
Sagrada Família: a temple that keeps changing
The Sagrada Família, Antoni Gaudí’s project, opened in 1882 and is still under construction. Each new stage adds unique details.
Inside the temple you can see light effects that change with the time of day, plus an exhibition telling the story of its construction.
Park Güell: a fairytale park of mosaics and sculptures
Park Güell, created by Gaudí, dazzles with bright mosaics and whimsical sculptures that seem to come alive in the sun.
The city park offers a panoramic view of Barcelona and cosy corners for walks and photos.
Casa Milà and Bunker Park: from a wave-like house to a hidden underground zone
Casa Milà, also known as La Pedrera, shows undulating walls and wrought-iron balconies, while the underground bunker holds a story of wartime defence.
Visitors can walk the underground corridors, see original artefacts and learn about the building’s role during the civil war.
Torre Agbar: a modern skyscraper that changes colour
Torre Agbar, designed by Jean Nouvel, changes colour thanks to LED lighting, creating a living façade effect.
The top floor has a restaurant with panoramic views, and at night the tower glows in shades of blue and pink.

articles.title: Top 5 things to do in Barcelona for an unforgettable trip
articles.lead: Barcelona is a city of contrasts where modern life meets history. Here’s what belongs on your itinerary.
articles.excerpt: From a stroll on La Rambla to a Gothic Quarter quest — five ideas to brighten your stay.

body.text: Barcelona is more than Gaudí — its lively streets are waiting to be explored.
Historic walks
Start the day with a walk along La Rambla, where you will find street musicians, flower stalls and the famous Boqueria market.
Immersion in art
Visit the Picasso Museum and enjoy a collection focused on his early work — a deep look at the city’s art and history.
Modern entertainment
Dive into a Barcelona quest room where you solve puzzles in the Gothic Quarter.
Do not miss an evening coastal cruise to see Barcelona’s night lights from the water.
